title: 299. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Recovering Transformation Parameters from Points
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(h\) in \(y=f(x-h)\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f\) be a one-to-one function with \(f(2)=5\). The graph of \(y=f(x-h)\) passes through \((4,5)\). What is \(h\)?
questions.explanation: The point \((4,5)\) on \(y=f(x-h)\) means \(f(4-h)=5\). Since \(f(2)=5\), we have \(f(4-h)=f(2)\). Because \(f\) is one-to-one, this implies \(4-h=2\). Solving gives \(h=2\).
questions.hint: Substitute the given point into the transformed equation and compare the input with the known input.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) in \(y=f(x)+k\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f(1)=3\). The graph of \(y=f(x)+k\) passes through \((1,7)\). What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x=1\), the graph gives \(f(1)+k=7\). Since \(f(1)=3\), we have \(3+k=7\). Therefore, \(k=4\).
questions.hint: Substitute the known function value into the transformed equation.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(a\) in \(y=a f(x)\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f(3)=6\). The graph of \(y=a f(x)\) passes through \((3,18)\). What is \(a\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x=3\), the graph gives \(a f(3)=18\). Since \(f(3)=6\), we have \(6a=18\). Therefore, \(a=3\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(f(3)=6\) into the equation and solve for \(a\).

questions.concept: Recovering a Horizontal Translation with a Vertical Translation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(h\) in \(y=f(x-h)+2\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f\) be a one-to-one function with \(f(0)=4\). The graph of \(y=f(x-h)+2\) passes through \((5,6)\). What is \(h\)?
questions.explanation:
Substitute \((5,6)\) into \(y=f(x-h)+2\):
\[
f(5-h)+2=6
\]
So \(f(5-h)=4\). Since \(f(0)=4\), we have \(f(5-h)=f(0)\). Because \(f\) is one-to-one, this implies \(5-h=0\). Therefore, \(h=5\).
questions.hint: First isolate \(f(x-h)\), then compare the input with the known input.

questions.concept: Recovering a Vertical Translation After Reflection
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) in \(y=-f(x)+k\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f(2)=7\). The graph of \(y=-f(x)+k\) passes through \((2,-3)\). What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x=2\), the graph gives \(-f(2)+k=-3\). Since \(f(2)=7\), we have \(-7+k=-3\). Therefore, \(k=4\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(f(2)=7\) into the equation and solve for \(k\).

questions.concept: Recovering a Horizontal Translation with a Vertical Translation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(h\) in \(y=f(x-h)-3\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f\) be a one-to-one function with \(f(4)=1\). The graph of \(y=f(x-h)-3\) passes through \((1,-2)\). What is \(h\)?
questions.explanation:
Substitute \((1,-2)\) into \(y=f(x-h)-3\):
\[
f(1-h)-3=-2
\]
So \(f(1-h)=1\). Since \(f(4)=1\), we have \(f(1-h)=f(4)\). Because \(f\) is one-to-one, this implies \(1-h=4\). Solving gives \(h=-3\).
questions.hint: Isolate \(f(x-h)\) first, then compare the input with the known input.

questions.concept: Recovering a Vertical Scaling and Translation Parameter
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(a\) in \(y=a f(x)+1\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f(5)=2\). The graph of \(y=a f(x)+1\) passes through \((5,9)\). What is \(a\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x=5\), the graph gives \(a f(5)+1=9\). Since \(f(5)=2\), we have \(2a+1=9\). Then \(2a=8\), so \(a=4\).
questions.hint: Substitute \(f(5)=2\) into the equation and solve for \(a\).

questions.concept: Recovering a Vertical Translation After Reflection Across the \(y\)-Axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) in \(y=f(-x)+k\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f(1)=6\). The graph of \(y=f(-x)+k\) passes through \((-1,10)\). What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: At \(x=-1\), the graph gives \(f(1)+k=10\). Since \(f(1)=6\), we have \(6+k=10\). Therefore, \(k=4\).
questions.hint: Evaluate \(f(-x)\) at the given \(x\)-value using the known function value.

questions.concept: Recovering a Horizontal Translation with Reflection and Scaling
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(h\) in \(y=-2f(x-h)\) from a given point and a known function value.
questions.question: Let \(f\) be a one-to-one function with \(f(2)=3\). The graph of \(y=-2f(x-h)\) passes through \((5,-6)\). What is \(h\)?
questions.explanation:
Substitute \((5,-6)\) into \(y=-2f(x-h)\):
\[
-2f(5-h)=-6
\]
Divide by \(-2\) to get \(f(5-h)=3\). Since \(f(2)=3\), we have \(f(5-h)=f(2)\). Because \(f\) is one-to-one, this implies \(5-h=2\). Solving gives \(h=3\).
questions.hint: First isolate \(f(x-h)\), then compare the input with the known input.

questions.concept: Recovering a Horizontal Translation from Two Points
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(h\) in \(y=f(x-h)\) from two points and known function values.
questions.question: Let \(f\) be a one-to-one function with \(f(1)=2\) and \(f(2)=5\). The graph of \(y=f(x-h)\) passes through \((3,2)\) and \((4,5)\). What is \(h\)?
questions.explanation: For the point \((3,2)\), we have \(f(3-h)=2\). Since \(f(1)=2\), we have \(f(3-h)=f(1)\). Because \(f\) is one-to-one, this implies \(3-h=1\), so \(h=2\). Checking the point \((4,5)\): \(f(4-h)=f(2)=5\), which is consistent. Therefore, \(h=2\).
questions.hint: Use either point to set the input of \(f\) equal to a known input, then solve for \(h\).
